notes: The athlete warning now checks YOUR sleep: set your wake-up and lights-out times in the new 😴 Sleep schedule (Hours tab) and the app judges a work plan by your real sleep — exact hours per night and your latest safe work end — instead of calling every 20+ hour week too heavy.
If a shift ends too late for your wind-down, the warning names the day and the exact minutes it costs your sleep. Leave the sleep times blank and the old hours-based caution stays.

You can now download your week: in the “Your week” view, tap 📸 Image to save or share a picture of your whole week — classes, practices, workouts + work, with totals and what it pays — or 📄 Text file for a plain-text copy you can paste anywhere.

Planning now runs off your class schedule end to end: the ✨ Suggest preview shows the full real pay for the plan — gross, every tax and deduction taken, your take-home, and about per month — using the same pay-stub math as your paycheck.
You can type your own target hours (like 22) next to the 12/16/20 chips, and a new “✨ Plan from my schedule” button in the planner jumps you straight to the suggestions.
Free days start at a friendlier time: a day with nothing scheduled — like Saturday — now starts its suggested shift at 10:00 AM instead of 7:00 AM.

Whole-app cleanup: everything tidied into comfortable, clearly-labeled cards so each thing is where you'd expect to find it — schedule, suggested hours, planner, break calendar and work log now sit in one clean order in the Hours tab, and the Budget summary leads its tab.
Roomier buttons and spacing everywhere: every tap target is a comfortable size, money figures line up neatly, and long names wrap instead of squeezing the layout on your phone.
Nothing about your numbers or how anything calculates has changed — same pay-stub math, same saved data, just a tidier app.

NEW 💵 Work Log pay breakdowns: open any logged week and tap "💵 Pay breakdown" to see that week's full pay picture — gross pay, every tax and deduction taken (federal, NY, Social Security, Medicare, 401K and the rest from your pay stub setup), total taken, and your exact take-home.
Weeks over 40 hours call out the overtime right in the breakdown — how many OT hours at 1.5× and how much extra gross they added.

NEW 📊 "Your records" now totals it all up: total gross logged and total taken (taxes + deductions) across every week you've logged, next to your hours and take-home totals. All of it is calculated with the same pay-stub math as the Paycheck tab, straight from the hours in your Work Log.

NEW 🗓️ Schedule tabs: the schedule card is now tabs — Classes / Practices / Workouts. Tap a tab, pick the days and start/end times, tap Add, then “add another” to keep going with more of the same — two classes in a row, then switch to Practices and put your practice times in.

NEW 💪 Workouts tab: solo training days get their own tab and their own times. They count toward busy days, ✨ Suggest my work hours routes around them, and the week view flags work that overlaps them — exactly like classes and practices.

The saved list now shows only the tab you're on, sorted by name, and tapping any entry in your week view jumps straight to editing it on its own tab. Everything you already saved carries over untouched.
NEW 🚫 Busy-day guard: if a day's classes + practice add up to 5+ hrs, ✨ Suggest my work hours now says "no work" for that day and puts the hours on your other days instead.

You can change the cutoff to 4h or 6h in the Suggest section — look for "Busy day = no work at". Days at or over the cutoff show why right in the preview: "🚫 no work — busy day (5 hrs 30 min of class + practice)".
The preview now says why every off day is off — "off — rest day" on Sundays, "off — meet day" on meet days. The guard only affects Suggest: your manual planner stays fully yours.

Practices count too: the Class Schedule form now has a Class / Practice toggle — add your practices with their start and end times (e.g. Track Practice, Mon/Wed/Fri 3:30–5:30 PM) and they appear in your week with a 🏃 marker, right alongside your classes.

✨ Suggest my work hours now routes around your practices exactly like your classes — same 30 minutes of breathing room before and after — and the week view's ⚠️ overlap warnings check your planned work shifts against practices too.

The schedule summary splits your load by kind — Classes: X / week · Practice: Y / week · Work planned — and adding a practice tags those days as Practice days in the planner, same as classes always have.
Classes you already saved carry over untouched — anything without a kind is treated as a class, exactly as before.
NEW ✨ Suggest my work hours in the Class Schedule: pick a weekly target — Light 12h, Typical 16h, or Max 20h — and the app fits work shifts around your classes for you.
Every shift keeps 30 minutes of breathing room before and after each class, Sundays and meet days stay off, and shifts run 2–6 hours between 7:00 AM and 10:00 PM.

You preview the whole suggested week first — if your classes only leave room for less than the target, it tells you. Nothing changes until you tap Apply, which drops the week into your school planner with real start/end times you can still edit day by day.

Exact times fixed: durations are now figured to the minute — a class or shift from 8:00 to 8:50 AM shows 50 min (0.83 hrs) instead of rounding down to 0.75 hrs. Hours you type keep their exact value too (0–12, to the minute).
NEW Class Schedule in the Hours tab: add as many classes as you have — a name, the days it meets, and its start and end times — and edit or delete any of them whenever your schedule changes.

Week view: your classes and your planned school-week work shifts side by side for the whole week, with ⚠️ overlap warnings whenever a work shift runs into a class, plus your total class time and planned work hours per week.
Adding a class also tags those days as Class days in the planner above, so your plan and your schedule stay in sync.

Type your hours in the Possible Hours planner — the sliders are gone. Every day in the school-week and break-week planners (and the selected day in the Break Calendar) is now a field: tap it and type, 0–12 hrs in quarter-hour steps.

Optional shift times per day: tap '+ times', set a start and an end, and the hours fill in from the shift length using the exact Paycheck-tab rule — 30 min unpaid meal on shifts over 6 hrs, paid breaks never subtracted. Type hours manually any time to override.

NEW Work Log in the Hours tab: log the hours you actually worked each week (type them day by day, set shift times, or copy your school plan in as worked) and look back at your records — most hours in a week with its date, average hours per week, total hours and total take-home logged, with per-day detail for every saved week.

Break countdown: the Break Calendar now shows a countdown chip for the break you're viewing — 'Starts in N days', 'Happening now — ends in N days', or 'Ended …' — and every saved break carries its own countdown tag ('starts in 23 days', '12 days left', 'done').

NEW Break Calendar in the Possible Hours tab: choose when your school break starts and when you return, and every day in between becomes a tappable calendar cell. Days start filled from your break-week pattern (Sundays off); tap to switch a day on or off and fine-tune its hours with steppers.

Whole-break pay estimate: total work days, total hours, gross and take-home for the entire break — figured week by week through the same pay-stub math as the Paycheck tab, with a per-week breakdown when a break spans multiple weeks.
Save multiple breaks by name (Winter Break, Spring Break…) and load or delete them anytime — everything stays on your device.

School weeks improved: one-tap Normal Week / Meet Week / Exam Week templates (Meet Week lightens Friday for travel and zeroes Saturday), Class / Practice / Meet tags on each day that persist with the plan, and a one-line load summary — Work Xh · Practice days: N · Meet: day.

NEW Possible Hours tab: a what-if week planner for students whose hours change with classes and track. Set the hours you could work each day (Mon–Sun) and see the week's gross and take-home using the exact same pay-stub math as the Paycheck tab.
School weeks and break weeks each keep their own saved plan — flip the toggle and both are remembered on your device.
One-tap scenarios — Light 12h, Typical 16h, Max 20h, Break week 28h — plus a compare strip showing weekly/monthly take-home and how fast each pace reaches your savings goal.
Athlete guardrails: school weeks over ~20 hrs get a gentle warning about sleep and recovery, and any single day over 8 hrs is flagged.
Donut center label reworked: "REMAINING" (small, muted gold) above the amount, "this month" below — cleaner than the old wording.
Donut center amount now auto-shrinks so large amounts fit inside the hole instead of overlapping the ring.
More breathing room above the donut label.
Tightened a couple of Budget tab wordings.
Fixed white bar behind the status bar on mobile.
Header title is now solid champagne — crisper, no washed-out gradient.
Earn tab: every option now links to its real signup site — tap a name to open it.

Sovereign visual rework: noir-lux banking theme — champagne gold (#d4af6a) on warm charcoal/near-black, hairline gold dividers, serif display numerals for the donut and all money figures, subtle film grain + vignette. True fullscreen on mobile: dynamic viewport (100dvh), edge-to-edge backgrounds, notch/safe-area padding on header, banners, and tab bar. Manifest display → fullscreen (falls back to standalone). CSS-only — all 8 tabs, paycheck math, Earn tab, Stocks, Discounts, and sync codes untouched.

NEW Earn tab: 29 dorm-friendly ways to make money in 6 groups (user testing sites, microtasks, freelance, selling, campus, gaming/PC) — each with a toggle and realistic monthly range, a live combined $/mo total bar, and one button that adds the midpoint as a separate side-income line (never touches paycheck math). Honest framing: $200–600/mo is a boost, not a paycheck replacement; second retail job, plasma, crypto/MLM/survey farms excluded.
Duotone visual rework: mint + amber accents on a deeper layered dark background — stronger hierarchy on every tab, richer cards, and tighter spacing.
Donut glow-up: soft halo behind the donut, slow rotating sheen (respects reduced-motion), larger on desktop.
Goal progress bar now fades mint to amber; result boxes get an accent rail; hints read as info strips.
Desktop sidebar active item gets an amber accent rail; bottom tab bar on phones is a tighter 7-item fit with a glowing active pill.
Full-width primary buttons and 46px+ inputs on phones; empty transaction lists show a friendly empty state. Everything works exactly as before.

Full visual rework: a premium dark fintech look — deeper layered backgrounds, a refined mint accent system, gradient cards and buttons, a glassy bottom tab bar on phones, polished inputs with glowing focus rings, and a richer header. Every feature works exactly as before.

New micro-details: gradient card titles with accent underlines, bolder money figures, smoother press feedback, and clearer focus states for keyboard users. All animations still respect your reduced-motion setting.
Home-screen logo now embedded directly in the app (same trick as StudyLens) — shows reliably when adding to Home Screen.
New home-screen logo: the app icon now shows properly on iPhone (was an SVG iOS ignores). Delete and re-add the home screen icon to see it.
Fixed: the donut center now shows the full amount with cents (e.g. $2,259.17) instead of rounding to whole dollars.

Mobile fit pass at 390px: all small buttons (chips, mini, delete) now reach the 44px tap target, the bottom tab bar is taller with more readable labels, checkboxes are bigger, the donut value shrinks for very long amounts so it never clips the circle, and long video/deal links wrap instead of pushing cards wider. PC layouts unchanged.
Fixed: the Install button could stay visible inside the installed app — the stylesheet was overriding the hide signal. The install prompt now reliably hides when installed and shows only on the web.

Hot-fix: the app's offline cache now always pulls fresh files from the network when a new version installs — the old installer could pack stale files into the new cache, which is how an update could leave you on the old build.

Fixed updates getting stuck: tapping Update now waits for the new version to actually install before reloading, and the update notice stays until the new version is confirmed running — no more 'latest version' while showing the old number. The footer version number is now written by the app itself, so it can never go stale.
Install prompt now hides completely when the app is installed — it only shows on the web.

Paycheck auto-detections: overtime is now automatic — hours over 40/week are paid at 1.5x and the breakdown says so. A new Auto-detections card shows your next payday (pick your payday weekday; add your last payday date for every-2-weeks pay) and flags odd inputs, like hours over 80/week, a rate below federal minimum wage, or deductions higher than your gross.

Donut fix (mobile): shows a subtle ring + helpful hint when there is nothing to chart yet instead of a blank hole; the 'left' slice is now a brighter green visible on the dark theme; the donut centers itself on phone screens.
Where-you-work picker (Paycheck tab): Walmart Digital Personal Shopper, Target, Amazon warehouse, McDonald's, or Custom — one tap sets your rate. Presets are starting points; the rate stays editable.

NEW Stocks tab (educational): watchlist with prices you type in yourself, price-history charts with highs and lows, an allocation calculator against your savings, and beginner investing videos. Paper-trading only — nothing moves real money, and this is not financial advice.
Device sync code (My Money tab): generate a one-time code on your phone, paste it on your PC, and everything moves over. No server, no account — copy/paste it yourself.

Deal Watchlist upgrade: store presets (Best Buy, Walmart, Amazon, Target, Newegg), per-item price history with a mini highs/lows chart, and a target-hit alert when the price you see hits your buy price.
Donut chart: tap any slice to see its category, amount, and share of the total; the center number pops up or down as your numbers change.
Fixed empty states: the goal celebration only fires when you set a real goal and reach it; with no income entered, the budget says so plainly instead of showing a $0.00 math chain.
New responsive layout: phones keep the single-column stacked cards with the bottom tab bar; PCs get a multi-column dashboard.

Shifts now track your paid 15-minute breaks: every shift starts with a 15-minute break and a 30-minute meal, shown right on the shift line. Breaks are paid, so they never reduce your paid hours. Old shifts pick up the 15-minute break automatically.

Savings goal date: the goal now recomputes on every keystroke — type hours, bills, or spending and the date moves right away. When you are saving, it says "You'll hit $X by [Month Year]" with the math. When spending eats the whole paycheck, it tells you exactly how short you are per month and how many extra hours/week would fix it — never a made-up date.

Deal Watchlist in Discount Finder: add an item + the price you would buy at. "Check price now" opens the store page; type the price you see and the app says Deal or Not yet, with a Last checked stamp and a Refresh deals button. Prices are ones you type — the app never pretends to check a store by itself.

State tax picker in the Paycheck tab: pick your state and the estimate uses that state's real 2025 standard deduction + brackets (single filer). States with no wage income tax come out $0. Federal uses the 2025 $15,000 standard deduction + 2025 brackets. If you entered a real pay stub, the stub numbers still win. Estimate only — not tax advice, no city/local tax.

Animations: money numbers count up when they change, the donut glides to its new shape, the goal bar fills smoothly, tabs fade in, buttons give a little press feedback. All of it turns off automatically if your device prefers reduced motion, and it stays light on phones.
Every number now shows how it was worked out — the take-home line shows your paid hours × rate → take-home/week → monthly, so you can check it yourself.
The Budget tab shows an “Updated HH:MM:SS” stamp that refreshes on every change, so you can see the numbers are live.
“Money I have right now” now says plainly whether it is using your typed number or following your My Money balances, with a Clear button to go back to following your balances.
Typing a bill amount or a shift meal break updates the budget right away instead of waiting until you tap away.
Fixed: a number once typed in “Money I have right now” used to keep overriding your balances with no visible sign — now the source is always shown.
Savings update your budget right away — typing your saved balance or checking balance updates “You’ll have left” immediately, no tab switch needed.
Phone layout — the top header no longer hides under the iPhone status bar, and the last card no longer hides behind the bottom tab bar.

Paycheck now shows every line from a real pay stub — federal tax, NY state tax, NY FLI, Social Security, Medicare, 401K, membership fee, company stock contribution, and stock purchase — each with a plain-words explanation.
Use my real pay stub — enter each line from your stub once and the app uses your real rates from then on. Reset to estimates anytime.
Your budget starts from the money you actually have — "Money I have right now" at the top of the Budget tab, filled in from your balances, editable in place.
Installable — tap "Install app" at the top of the Budget tab to add it to your phone or PC home screen. Works offline once installed.
Everyone starts blank — your numbers stay on your own device only. Nobody else sees them.
What's New actually shows the notes now — the box used to open empty.
Typing a category amount no longer kicks you out of the box after each number.
Bills can now be edited in place — name, amount, due date, and auto-pay — instead of delete-and-retype.
Switching between Total hours and My shifts no longer wipes the tip calculator's %.
New rate box says plainly to type a rate instead of showing $0.00.
New: Check for updates button in the footer.
Balances no longer start with a made-up date — empty until you set it.
Dark background — easier on the eyes, day and night.
Bank statement import — drop in a CSV from your bank and the app fills in your balance. Nothing leaves your device, no bank login.
Meal breaks count — shifts over 6 hours start with a 30-minute unpaid meal break, taken off your paid hours.
Simpler to read — plain words, one main action per tab, extra details tucked behind “Show details”.
Update notices — the app tells you when a new version is out, once per version.
Polished on PC and phone.
First version — budget donut, paycheck calculator with tax breakdown, My Money, bills, discount finder, and calculators.
